title: National flu and COVID-19 surveillance report: 19 November 2026 (week 47) - GOV.UK

analysis.time: The report is based on data up to week 46 of 2026 (9 November to 15 November 2026) and was published on 19 November 2026.
analysis.location_and_population: England, with data on influenza, RSV, and COVID-19 activity across different age groups and populations, including those aged 75 years and over, individuals with weakened immune systems, and school-aged children.
analysis.event: The report indicates that influenza activity increased and is circulating at low levels, with ED attendances for influenza-like-illness above seasonally expected levels. It also notes that vaccine uptake is lower among certain age groups and clinical risk groups compared to the previous season.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: Influenza-confirmed ARI incidents increased compared with the previous week. Vaccine uptake is lower among patients aged 65 years and over (65.8% vs 67.8%), patients aged 6 months to under 65 years in clinical risk groups (32.5% vs 33.5%), those aged 2 years (37.6% vs 38.5%), and those aged 3 years (37.5% vs 38.8%).
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: A briefing note has been issued to inform the NHS about influenza activity. The report uses the moving epidemic method (MEM) and mean standard deviation method (MSD) to define thresholds, and these methods are experimental and may be subject to future revision. The data is provisional and subject to retrospective updates.

analysis.brief_en: The National Flu and COVID-19 Surveillance Report for 19 November 2026 (week 47) highlights that influenza activity in England increased during week 46, with emergency department attendances for influenza-like-illness (ILI) above seasonally expected levels. The report notes that influenza-confirmed acute respiratory infection (ARI) incidents rose compared to the previous week. Vaccine uptake among certain groups, such as those aged 65 years and over, patients in clinical risk groups, and those aged 2 and 3 years, was lower than the previous season. However, uptake among pregnant women was higher. The report also mentions that RSV activity increased, while COVID-19 activity remained stable. The data is based on the Moving Epidemic Method (MEM) and Mean Standard Deviation Method (MSD), which are experimental and may be revised. The report warns that testing policies and practices can affect positivity rates, and data is provisional, subject to updates. The findings are based on surveillance systems capturing test results from laboratories in England.
analysis.summary_en: The National Flu and COVID-19 Surveillance Report for 19 November 2026 (week 47) highlights that influenza activity in England increased during week 46, with emergency department attendances for influenza-like-illness (ILI) above seasonally expected levels. However, uptake among pregnant women was higher. The report also mentions that RSV activity increased, while COVID-19 activity remained stable.
